recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first browser canvas game called **Alien Tide Legend: Crystal Cave Sequence**. Preserve the source mechanic exactly: a timed ordered sequence is shown, the same items shuffle into a lower pool, the player taps items into the first open slot, can tap slotted items back out, and the game checks automatically when all slots are filled. Correct order adds score and advances the tide; incorrect order triggers wipeout/game-over. Rebuild all presentation as an alien crystal cave surf legend with procedural cave crystals, wave lines, surfboard-like numbered glyphs, PEARLS score language, TIDE progression, and mobile-readable HUD.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Game Truth
- genre: mobile-first canvas memory-order sequence puzzle
- objective: memorize a short ordered row of numbered tiles, then tap shuffled tiles back into empty slots in the same order
- input model: pointer/touch taps on canvas tiles; tapping pool tiles places them into the first empty slot; tapping slotted tiles returns them to the pool; restart button/canvas tap after game-over resets
- core loop: show sequence for a timed memorize phase, shuffle tiles to the lower pool, accept tap placement, auto-check when all slots are filled, award score and advance on correct order, game-over on wrong order
- fail/friction state: a wrong completed sequence shakes tiles, plays fail feedback, then opens the game-over/restart overlay

## Protected Mechanics
- timed memorize phase using base time plus time per tile
- sequence length scaling from 3 up to 6 using the source count formula
- unique numeric glyph values per round
- tap-to-place first-empty-slot behavior and tap-to-return behavior
- automatic checking once all slots are occupied
- score increment of 100 + level * 50, level increment on success, game-over on incorrect sequence

## Safe Remix Surfaces
HUD vocabulary, title, score labels, tile silhouettes, particle visuals, background, fonts, colors, audio labels, state messages, feedback flashes, and progression names are all presentation-facing and safe to transform.
